question: Within a simulated continuous double auction with price-time priority and cash and inventory constraints, does replacing 30% of random-order traders by trend followers change the volatility clustering of mid-price returns, and is any change attributable to price feedback rather than to aggressiveness, the sampling interval or the tick size?
status_label: Frozen verdict: invalidated (EXP-001, sign reversal under the EXP-004 robustness rule). Preregistered simulation study; independent preprint draft, not peer-reviewed.

experiments.title: Agent mixtures and volatility clustering (primary hypothesis H1)
experiments.verdict: invalidated (a sign reversal with an interval excluding 0), under the frozen EXP-004 robustness rule; the primary contrast alone is inconclusive (H1 not supported)

estimates.label: VCI(A2) - VCI(A0), mean reverters (secondary, Holm interval)

notes: 30 paired seeds, d_z -0.121. An inconclusive result is not evidence of no effect.

Secondary reading only (exploratory, E4): with the sign of H1 as the reference, the same rule would return "qualified" rather than "invalidated". Both readings agree that the answer depends on the sampling interval.

experiments.title: Liquidity supply and spread

estimates.label: interaction on VCI, [med-ZI+TF - med-ZI] - [high-ZI+TF - high-ZI] (secondary, Holm interval)

notes: The pre-declared low-ZI+TF arm was degenerate in 30 of 30 runs (model failure for that arm) and is excluded from every contrast.
The interaction may reflect discreteness at a spread close to one tick rather than an interplay between liquidity and trend feedback.

experiments.title: Response to an exogenous sell shock (optional)
experiments.status: confirmatory, optional; complete (M3 2026-11-25; optional, run in full)
notes: In 7 of 30 trend-follower runs the mid did not return within 1% of the pre-shock level within 20,000 steps (censored).

experiments.title: Sensitivity analyses that could invalidate EXP-001
experiments.verdict: robustness rule: invalidated (a sign reversal with an interval excluding 0); placebo contrast contradicted, attribution rule not triggered (EXP-001 inconclusive)
notes: The rule calls EXP-001 robust only if every dt and tick component has the same sign as EXP-001 and an interval excluding 0. The sign reference is the near-zero EXP-001 point estimate (D-013), so its sign is weakly determined (D-015).
The six EXP-004 components carry no multiplicity adjustment; the placebo interval's upper end is close to 0.

arm A1 mean VCI against FI-2010 range: overlapping

notes: Single stock-days give noisy VCI estimates; no interval is reported for them.
The placement is descriptive, depends on a crude clock match, and is never a validation of the model or a statement about real markets.

assumptions.name: Market
assumptions.value: one asset, continuous double auction with price-time priority; trades at the resting order's price; no fees, latency or hidden orders

assumptions.name: Price grid
assumptions.value: integer prices, tick 1 (tick 2 in the EXP-004 tick arms); initial price 1,000; price floor of one tick

assumptions.name: Time
assumptions.value: event time: T = 100,000 steps, one of 100 agents drawn uniformly per step; first B = 10,000 steps are burn-in

assumptions.name: Accounting
assumptions.value: cash and inventory never negative (no short selling, no borrowing); endowment 1,000,000 cash and 1,000 units per agent

assumptions.name: Random-order (ZI) agent
assumptions.value: market order with probability 0.2, otherwise a limit order 0 to 10 ticks behind the best opposite quote; sizes uniform on 1 to 5 units

assumptions.name: Trend follower (TF)
assumptions.value: direction sign(m_t - m_{t-500}); no order when the signal is 0; market order with probability 0.5, else a limit order at its own best quote

assumptions.name: Mean reverter (MR)
assumptions.value: direction -sign(m_t - MA_500(m)_t), same order rule as TF

assumptions.name: Placebo aggressive (PA)
assumptions.value: TF order types and sizes, direction from a fair coin independent of prices

assumptions.name: Order lifetime
assumptions.value: every resting order expires after 2,000 steps

assumptions.name: Primary metric
assumptions.value: VCI = mean autocorrelation of absolute mid-price log returns at lags 1 to 10, returns sampled every dt = 50 steps after burn-in

assumptions.name: Seeds and analysis
assumptions.value: confirmatory seeds 1001 to 1030 shared across arms (common random numbers); paired differences with 95% percentile bootstrap intervals (10,000 resamples)

assumptions.name: Frozen configuration
assumptions.value: Frozen v1.0 (owner-approved 2026-11-24). SimConfig defaults are the frozen parameter values of protocol EXP-001 section 7. 30 seeds (amendment A2).

limitations: VCI is one statistic. In this model it is shaped by bid-ask bounce at short sampling intervals and by trend runs at long intervals, so it is not a clean measure of volatility clustering.
The EXP-004 verdict depends on an analysis choice: with the sign of H1 as the reference, the robustness rule returns "qualified" instead of the frozen "invalidated".
A1's VCI varies widely across seeds, so the primary test had low power for the effect that occurred; a null result is not evidence of no effect.
Replacing random-order agents by trend followers also changes depth and spread; the placebo matches order types, sizes and activity but not the serial correlation of direction.
One parameter set, 100 fixed-rule agents, one asset, self-trades allowed, a one-tick price floor; the model is not calibrated to any market.
The FI-2010 comparison covers five Helsinki stocks over ten days in 2010 with a crude clock match; it is descriptive only.
The exploratory checks were designed after the confirmatory results were seen; they are hypothesis-generating only.
Nothing here is a statement about real markets, a prediction, trading advice or a claim of profitability.

headline.frozen_text: Under the frozen protocol, the primary interpretation is invalidated: EXP-001 is invalidated by a sign reversal under the frozen EXP-004 robustness rule. Trend followers did not detectably change volatility clustering at the preregistered interval of 50 steps, and the contrast was positive, with intervals excluding 0, at 10 and 200 steps.
headline.secondary_text: As a secondary reading only, taking the sign of H1 as the reference would make the same rule return "qualified" rather than "invalidated". Both readings agree that the answer depends on the sampling interval.

not_measured.outcome: spread widening after the shock (declared secondary outcome)
not_measured.reason: the protocol gives no formula and no metric is defined after the data (owner decision, D-015)
